questions.title: Which country will announce a new multinational maritime coalition to protect navigation through the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden by August 1, 2026?
questions.background: Attacks on commercial shipping since 2023 have heightened concerns about the security of maritime trade routes through the Red Sea.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official government announcements or contemporaneous reporting by reputable international news organizations. Resolution Conditions : Identify the country that announces the creation of a new multinational maritime coalition between July 1 and August 1, 2026, inclusive, with a stated purpose of protecting freedom of navigation through the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb Strait and Gulf of Aden. Joining an existing coalition does not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: No country has announced a new Red Sea/Bab al-Mandeb/Gulf of Aden multinational maritime coalition through 2026-07-15, but sharp July 13-15 regional escalation materially strengthens the case for a Saudi- or Egyptian-led initiative over a US-led one. On July 15 (Irish Times, Straits Times/Reuters), following the US's renewed Iran naval blockade and Houthi ballistic missile strikes on Saudi Arabia that broke the four-year Yemen truce, Iran's IRGC threatened to close 'all other export corridors that benefit the US and its allies'—putting Saudi Arabia's Red Sea Yanbu export bypass and Bab al-Mandeb directly in the crosshairs after Houthi officials warned of closing Bab al-Mandeb in an 'operational alliance' with Hormuz. Simultaneously, Reuters reported July 15 that commercial shipping companies are refusing US military-guided Hormuz transits after five vessel attacks since July 7—reducing the appeal and diplomatic feasibility of a brand-new US-branded coalition (especially since Operation Prosperity Guardian already exists and US forces are tied down fighting Iran). Lifting Saudi Arabia 0.20 -> 0.24 (leader of the Red Sea Council with existential Yanbu stakes) and Egypt 0.16 -> 0.17 (Suez Canal exposure, CTF 153 commander), trimming United States 0.14 -> 0.12, and holding United Kingdom (0.10) and France (0.09), leaving 28% residual for China, India, UAE, Greece, Bahrain, Turkey, Italy, or others.

questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Contemporaneous reporting by Al Jazeera, supported where available by official military statements. questions.background: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) carries out arrests as part of federal immigration enforcement.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Use government data supplied by ICE, as reported by The Associated Press. Resolution Date : Resolve to the calendar month of 2026 with the largest arrest total among the months covered by the latest ICE monthly figures publicly available by August 26, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the month name only.
questions.current_reasoning: Major June 25-July 14 update combining three critical developments (AP News July 2 & July 14, NYT/Daily Beast July 2 & July 14, CBS/HT July 14): (1) Late-June arrest surge — Trump quietly ordered a 2,000/day arrest benchmark, and ICE arrested >10,000 people in a 5-day period at the end of June (peaking >2,400 on June 27, pushing detention up ~4,000 to >63,000), vaulting June's full-month total into the ~36k-40k range right alongside January's ~38k-39k high-water mark (lifting June 0.17 -> 0.24); (2) July started at that ~2,000/day surge pace for July 1-13, giving July major upside (>40k full month) if reported by August 26, though tempered by ICE's July 14 temporary suspension of most ERO routine vehicle stops for training following fatal shootings in Houston (July 7) and Biddeford, Maine (July 13) (lifting July 0.15 -> 0.21); (3) Critical data-lag constraint — AP's July 14 wire explicitly noted that ICE arrest data provided to UC Berkeley's Deportation Data Project and analyzed by AP still only ran through March 11, 2026 ('the most recent data available'). Substantial ~25-30% risk that June/July monthly figures are not yet publicly available by August 26, plus January's strong ~38k-39k benchmark even if June is released, keeps January #1 at 0.48 (down from 0.56), while trimming pre-surge lull months May (0.07 -> 0.03) and March (0.03 -> 0.02), leaving 2% for April/February/August.

questions.title: Which international organization, if any, will first gain direct access to Aung San Suu Kyi in detention during 2026?
questions.background: Aung San Suu Kyi has been detained since Myanmar's military overthrew her government in February 2021. Her access to outside visitors has been tightly restricted.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements from the visiting organization or Myanmar authorities, corroborated by established news reporting. Qualifying Event : Direct access means a completed in-person meeting with Suu Kyi by a representative acting on behalf of an international organization. Permission or an announced plan without a completed visit does not qualify. Resolution : Resolve to the first international organization publicly confirmed to have completed such a visit during 2026. If no qualifying visit is confirmed by December 31, 2026, resolve that no organization qualified. Accepted Answer Format : The organization's name, or a statement that no organization qualified.
questions.current_reasoning: Significant 2026-07-12 diplomatic update from Bangkok (Straits Times/Reuters): ASEAN foreign ministers held their first in-person meeting with Myanmar's Foreign Minister Tin Maung Swe since the 2021 coup, yet Myanmar granted zero access to Aung San Suu Kyi and offered only verbal assurances that she is 'in good health' and treated like a 'sister'. Reporting explicitly notes that calls and a recent ASEAN member-state request to meet her have been ignored or turned down, while analysts warn that Min Aung Hlaing's diplomatic normalization (visits to India, China, ASEAN member Laos on July 3-5, and now Bangkok without concessions) plus China-brokered battlefield gains reduce Naypyitaw's incentive to concede access. With >53% of 2026 elapsed and over five years of unbroken refusal, 'No organization qualified' rises 0.44 -> 0.52. Conditionally, if any organization does secure a visit in H2 2026 to unlock further ASEAN normalization, ASEAN's share strengthens sharply (0.25 -> 0.26 despite lower overall P(visit)) because Special Envoy Ma. Theresa Lazaro plans an H2 humanitarian mission to Myanmar and Thai FM Sihasak explicitly pressed for Lazaro to meet Suu Kyi, whereas ICRC (0.21 -> 0.14) and UN (0.07 -> 0.05) show no active traction; WHO holds at 0.01.
